answer: Timed challenges force a farm to buy one machine per 3 keys. Each epoch every key must return a 20-second sequential hash task, the kernel, issued at a random second inside a 60-second window, so one machine finishes only 3 tasks. A wharf, the public verifier queue, rejects late results, and a key that misses 2 epochs enters the glacier, a 10-epoch freeze that pays nothing. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 334 machines at 30 POA rental per epoch. Attacker pays 334 x 30 POA = 10,020 POA per epoch.
